newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Jan 31.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- University lecturers' strike over campus tension between the authorities and student activists was only partly followed - Half vehicles on roads in Ivory Coast are breaking the law as they do not have roadworthiness certificate, the head of the SICTA testing agency says
- Pharmacies are angry with civil service medical insurance mutual saying it has not been reimbursing them for medicines given to its members; some pharmacies refuse to accept its vouchers
- Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan attends international development forum in Davos, Switzerland
- Major Ivorian agro-industrial companies using cotton or palm oil as a raw material complain of supply problems
- Ivory Coast's privatised companies plan investments totalling more than 430 billion CFA over the next five years.
- Agro-industrial company BLOHORN announces 7.29 percent increase in turnover in financial year ending September 30 1996.

- First day of strike called by university lecturers union SYNARES largely followed; union called 48-hour strike after death of student following university residence clash between students and security forces

- Villagers issue statement opposing sale of Dabou Savannah rubber and palm oil plantations as part of privatisation of Ivorian agro-industrial giant Palmindustrie; seek audience with President Henri Konan Bedie, saying the plantations are on their land
- Sacked former army chief of staff General Robert Guei, thrown out of the army by the government on Wednesday, refused to appear before special military investigating tribunal

- Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze says Africa will cut its coffee export quota by 850,000 60-kg sacks as part of efforts to boost world prices; producing countries seek total cut of 1,300,000 60-kg sacks.
